title: Quantizing weights and the cache
summary: PTQ versus QAT, and what GPTQ, AWQ, FP8, and KV quantization each change.

choices.text: At long context the KV cache can exceed the weights, so quantizing K and V is a separate lever from quantizing the weight matrices. The rounding error is reread on later steps.
FP8 is INT8 under another name: both store 8-bit integers with one scale per tensor, so any INT8 kernel can run an FP8 checkpoint unchanged.
INT4 weight post-training quantization and quantization-aware training produce the same weights, because both round to the same grid; QAT only adds a calibration set.
Post-training quantization compresses a finished model, sometimes with a small calibration set. Quantization-aware training simulates the rounding while training so the weights can adapt to it.

GPTQ is a post-training method that quantizes weights layer by layer and uses second-order (Hessian) information to compensate for the rounding. AWQ is a post-training method that protects the weight channels that multiply large activations.
